title: APEX-Harm: Evaluating Agent Safety in Shared Professional Workspaces
abstract: arXiv:2610.13623v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Professional agents increasingly work through command-line interfaces and multiple tools over shared workspaces containing files, messages, and business applications. These environments create safety risks that are difficult to capture with attacks placed at a single, known read location. We introduce APEX-Harm, a benchmark for evaluating prompt and script injection against long-horizon agents performing finance, consulting, and legal tasks in large workspaces. Each task contains 115 to 328 files, together with email, calendar, chat, document, spreadsheet, PDF, and code-execution tools exposed through MCP servers. The benchmark includes six attack categories covering static and dynamic injections, task-specific script replacement, and attacker-provided generic scripts, and evaluates attack success, exposure, and task performance. We evaluate 12 frontier models on 180 task instances per model. Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 have the lowest overall

translated_title: APEX-Harm：评估共享专业工作空间中的智能体安全性
translated_abstract: 专业智能体越来越多地通过命令行界面和多种工具，在包含文件、消息和业务应用的共享工作空间中开展工作。这类环境带来的安全风险，难以通过放置在单一已知读取位置的攻击来捕捉。我们提出了APEX-Harm，这是一个用于评估提示注入和脚本注入攻击的基准测试，针对的是在大型工作空间中执行金融、咨询和法律任务的长时程智能体。每个任务包含115到328个文件，并配有通过MCP服务器暴露的电子邮件、日历、聊天、文档、电子表格、PDF和代码执行工具。该基准涵盖六类攻击，包括静态与动态注入、任务特定脚本替换以及攻击者提供的通用脚本，并从攻击成功率、暴露程度和任务性能三个维度进行评估。我们在每个模型180个任务实例上评估了12个前沿模型。Opus 5和Sonnet 5的总体（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了APEX-Harm基准，在包含上百个文件和多种工具的共享专业工作空间中，通过六类提示与脚本注入攻击评估执行金融、咨询和法律任务的长时程智能体的安全性，对12个前沿模型的测试显示其仍存在显著安全风险。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces APEX-Harm, a benchmark that evaluates prompt and script injection attacks against long-horizon professional agents performing finance, consulting, and legal tasks in large shared workspaces, revealing that 12 frontier models still exhibit notable safety vulnerabilities.
